findings.detail: The 110-per-share value takes one reported quarter of 120000000 net income four times. That is a legitimate estimate, but the draft's rationale presents the resulting yield as if it were a demonstrated full-year record. Say plainly that the run-rate is one quarter old and that 2026-10-20 is its first test.
findings.title: The value arithmetic annualizes a single quarter without saying so plainly

findings.detail: The record cannot say whether the reported profit converts to cash. If capital spending consumes a large share of net income, the earnings yield behind the cheap reading is overstated. Consider whether a view should wait for the figure.
findings.title: The unpriced free-cash-flow gap deserves more than a mention

findings.summary: A coherent, priced draft on an honest record. The rating is defensible at buy; the conviction language runs slightly ahead of a one-quarter record, and the free-cash-flow hole is named but not weighed. Nothing here overturns the thesis; two findings ask the chairman to earn his wording. (Invented fixture text.)
